We propose a study that uses mother as a bridge: first, review how district and labor supply are each currently treated through mother; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
quant-1217-2473.phd: A 3-4 year programme building a unified framework for district and labor supply. Year 1: systematic review of the 180 shared concepts (starting with mother, turning point and deviation increase); years 2-3: develop and validate a joint method; year 4: generalise it and release open tools and data.
quant-1217-2473.masters: A 6-12 month project: reproduce one recent district study and one recent labor supply study, then run a focused experiment combining the two through mother, reporting what transfers and what does not.
quant-1217-2473.industry: Illustrative example only (no claim about the firm's actual work): an industry research team such as Marshall Wace could run a short feasibility study testing whether combining district with labor supply via mother adds measurable value to an existing quant pipeline, then decide whether to invest further.
